readings.title: The Wages of the Shepherd
readings.subtitle: Jacob's Flocks Multiply
readings.text: [Genesis 30:25] And it came to be, when Raḥěl had borne <dn>את</dn> Yosěph, that Ya‛aqoḇ said to Laḇan, “Send me on my way, to go to my own place and to my land. [26] “Give <dn>את</dn> my wives and <dn>את</dn> my children for whom I have served you, and let me go, for you yourself know <dn>את</dn> my service which I have done for you.” [27] And Laḇan said to him, “If I have found favour in your eyes, please stay, for I have diligently watched that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed me for your sake.” [28] And he said, “Name me your wages, and I give it.” [29] So he said to him, “You know <dn>את</dn> how I have served you and <dn>את</dn> how your livestock has been with <dn>את</dn> me. [30] “For the little you had before I came has increased greatly, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed you since my coming. But now, when am I to provide for my own house too?” [31] And he said, “What do I give you?” And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “Give me naught! If you do this for me, I shall again feed and guard your flocks: [32] “Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there all the speckled and spotted sheep, and all the black ones among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. And these shall be my wages. [33] “And my righteousness shall answer for me in time to come, when you come concerning my wages: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the lambs, it is stolen if it is with me.” [34] And Laḇan said, “See, let it be according to your word!” [35] And on that day he set aside <dn>את</dn> the male goats that were speckled and spotted, and <dn>את</dn> all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had some white in it, and all the black ones among the lambs, and gave them into the hand of his sons. [36] And he put three days’ journey between himself and Ya‛aqoḇ, and Ya‛aqoḇ fed <dn>את</dn> the rest of Laḇan’s flocks. [37] And Ya‛aqoḇ took for himself rods of green poplar and of the almond and chestnut trees, peeled white strips in them, and exposed the white which was in the rods. [38] And he set <dn>את</dn> the rods which he had peeled before the flocks in the gutters, in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink, and they conceived when they came to drink. [39] So the flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks brought forth streaked, speckled, and spotted. [40] And Ya‛aqoḇ separated <dn>את</dn> the lambs, and made the flocks face toward the streaked and all the black in the flock of Laḇan, but he put his own flocks by themselves and did not put them with Laḇan’s flock. [41] And it came to be, whenever the strong ones of the flock conceived, that Ya‛aqoḇ placed <dn>את</dn> the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, so they would conceive among the rods. [42] But when the flocks were weak, he did not put them in, so the weak ones were Laḇan’s and the strong ones Ya‛aqoḇ’s. [43] Thus the man increased very much, and had many flocks, and female and male servants, and camels and donkeys.

readings.title: The Flight from Paddan Aram
readings.subtitle: Jacob Departs in Secret
readings.text: [Genesis 31:1] And he heard <dn>את</dn> the words of Laḇan’s sons, saying, “Ya‛aqoḇ has taken away <dn>את</dn> all that was our father’s, and from what belonged to our father he has made <dn>את</dn> all this wealth.” [2] And Ya‛aqoḇ would look at <dn>את</dn> the face of Laḇan and see that it was not toward him as before. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives. And <dn>I</dn> am with you.”</dq> [4] And Ya‛aqoḇ sent and called Raḥěl and Lě’ah to the field, to his flock, [5] and said to them, “I see <dn>את</dn> your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before, but the <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father has been with me. [6] “And you know that I have served <dn>את</dn> your father with all my strength. [7] “Yet your father has deceived me and changed <dn>את</dn> my wages ten times, but <dn>Elohim</dn> did not allow him to do evil to me. [8] “When he said this, ‘The speckled are your wages,’ then all the flocks bore speckled. And when he said this, ‘The streaked are your wages,’ then all the flocks bore streaked. [9] “So <dn>Elohim</dn> has taken away <dn>את</dn> the livestock of your father and given them to me. [10] “And it came to be, at the time when the flocks conceived, that I lifted my eyes and looked in a dream and saw the rams which leaped upon the flocks were streaked, speckled, and mottled. [11] “And the Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to me in a dream, saying, <dq>‘Ya‛aqoḇ.’</dq> And I said, ‘Here I am.’ [12] “And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>‘Lift your eyes now and see, all the rams which leap on the flocks are streaked, speckled, and mottled, for <dn>I</dn> have seen all that Laḇan is doing to you.</dq> [13] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Ěl</dn> of Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, where you anointed the standing column and where you made a vow to <dn>Me</dn>. Now rise up, get out of this land, and return to the land of your relatives.’</dq> ” [14] And Raḥěl and Lě’ah answered and said to him, “Do we still have any portion or inheritance in our father’s house? [15] “Are we not reckoned by him as strangers? For he has sold us, and also entirely consumed <dn>את</dn> our silver. [16] “For all the wealth which <dn>Elohim</dn> has taken from our father is ours and our children’s. Now then, do whatever <dn>Elohim</dn> has told you.” [17] So Ya‛aqoḇ rose and put <dn>את</dn> his sons and <dn>את</dn> his wives on camels, [18] and he drove off <dn>את</dn> all his livestock and <dn>את</dn> all his possessions which he had acquired, his property of the livestock which he had acquired in Paddan Aram, to go to his father Yitsḥaq in the land of Kena‛an. [19] And when Laḇan had gone to shear his sheep, Raḥěl stole <dn>את</dn> the house idols that were her father’s. [20] And Ya‛aqoḇ deceived <dn>את</dn> Laḇan the Aramean, because he did not inform him that he was about to flee. [21] And he fled with all that he had. And he rose up and passed over <dn>את</dn> the river, and headed toward the mountains of Gil‛aḏ.

readings.title: The Pursuit and Confrontation
readings.subtitle: Laban Overtakes Jacob in Gilead
readings.text: [Genesis 31:22] And on the third day Laḇan was told that Ya‛aqoḇ had fled. [23] Then he took <dn>את</dn> his brothers with him and pursued him for seven days’ journey, and he overtook him in the mountains of Gil‛aḏ. [24] But in a dream by night <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Laḇan the Aramean, and said to him, <dq>“Guard yourself, that you do not speak to Ya‛aqoḇ either good or evil.”</dq> [25] Then Laḇan overtook <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ. Now Ya‛aqoḇ had pitched his tent in the mountains, and Laḇan with <dn>את</dn> his brothers pitched in the mountains of Gil‛aḏ. [26] And Laḇan said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and driven <dn>את</dn> my daughters off like captives taken with the sword? [27] “Why did you flee secretly and deceive me, and not inform me, and I would have sent you away with joy and songs, with tambourine and lyre? [28] “And you did not allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have been foolish to do this. [29] “It is in the power of my hand to do evil to you, but the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father spoke to me last night, saying, <dq>‘Guard yourself, that you do not speak to Ya‛aqoḇ either good or evil.’</dq> [30] “And now you have gone because you greatly long for your father’s house, but why did you steal <dn>את</dn> my mighty ones?” [31] And Ya‛aqoḇ answered and said to Laḇan, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you tear <dn>את</dn> your daughters away from me.’ [32] “With whomever you find <dn>את</dn> your mighty ones, do not let him live. In the presence of our brothers, see for yourself what is with me and take it with you.” For Ya‛aqoḇ did not know that Raḥěl had stolen them. [33] And Laḇan went into Ya‛aqoḇ’s tent, and into Lě’ah’s tent, and into the tents of the two female servants, but he did not find them. And he came out of Lě’ah’s tent and entered Raḥěl’s tent. [34] Now Raḥěl had taken <dn>את</dn> the house idols and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. And Laḇan searched <dn>את</dn> all about the tent but did not find them. [35] And she said to her father, “Let it not displease my master that I am unable to rise before you, for the way of women is with me.” And he searched but did not find <dn>את</dn> the house idols. [36] And Ya‛aqoḇ was wroth and contended with Laḇan, and Ya‛aqoḇ answered and said to Laḇan, “What is my transgression? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me? [37] “Now that you have searched <dn>את</dn> all my goods what have you found of all your household goods? Set it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them decide between the two of us! [38] “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried their young, and I have not eaten the rams of your sheep. [39] “That which was torn by beasts I did not bring to you, I myself bore the loss of it. You required it from my hand, whether stolen by day or stolen by night. [40] “Thus I was! By day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes. [41] “These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed <dn>את</dn> my wages ten times. [42] “Unless the <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham and the Fear of Yitsḥaq, had been with me, you would now have sent me away empty-handed. <dn>Elohim</dn> has seen <dn>את</dn> my affliction and <dn>את</dn> the labour of my hands, and rendered judgment last night.”

readings.title: The Covenant of Galeed
readings.subtitle: A Witness Between Jacob and Laban
readings.text: [Genesis 31:43] And Laḇan answered and said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and this flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine. But what shall I do today to these, my daughters or to their children whom they have borne? [44] “And now, come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and it shall be a witness between you and me.” [45] So Ya‛aqoḇ took a stone and set it up as a standing column. [46] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his brothers, “Gather stones.” And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there on the heap. [47] And Laḇan called it Yeḡar Sahaḏutha, but Ya‛aqoḇ called it Gal‛ěḏ. [48] And Laḇan said, “This heap is a witness between you and me today.” That is why its name was called Gal‛ěḏ, [49] also Mitspah, because he said, “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> watch between you and me when we are out of each other’s sight. [50] “If you afflict <dn>את</dn> my daughters, or if you take other wives besides my daughters, although no man is with us; see, <dn>Elohim</dn> is witness between you and me!” [51] And Laḇan said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “See this heap and see this standing column, which I have placed between you and me. [52] “This heap is a witness, and this standing column is a witness, that I do not pass beyond <dn>את</dn> this heap to you, and you do not pass beyond <dn>את</dn> this heap and <dn>את</dn> this standing column to me, for evil. [53] “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Naḥor, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of their father rightly rule between us!” And Ya‛aqoḇ swore by the Fear of his father Yitsḥaq. [54] And Ya‛aqoḇ slaughtered a slaughtering on the mountain, and called his brothers to eat bread. And they ate bread and spent the night on the mountain. [55] And Laḇan rose up early in the morning, and kissed his sons and daughters and blessed <dn>את</dn> them. And Laḇan left and returned to his place.
